notes: All acquisitions, orbit/frame identifiers, events, metrics, and textures are fictional illustrations.
Coordinates identify real geographic areas; samples make no claims about changes there.
Earthquake analysis illustrates GUNW interferometry, not GCOV.

phenomena.label: Wetland loss
phenomena.explanation: Radar responds to water, vegetation, and surface roughness. Amber patches illustrate a decrease in backscatter between acquisitions. A shift in the distribution can flag areas for closer review.
phenomena.limitation: A backscatter decrease is not proof of wetland loss. Water level, season, and viewing geometry also change the signal.

phenomena.label: Earthquakes
phenomena.explanation: Interferometry compares radar phase between repeat passes to estimate movement toward or away from the satellite. The colors illustrate displacement; the profile follows movement across a sample fault corridor.
phenomena.limitation: Illustrative GUNW-style analysis, not a real earthquake or warning. GCOV cannot measure displacement. Atmospheric effects and phase unwrapping affect real estimates.

phenomena.label: Deforestation
phenomena.explanation: L-band radar is sensitive to forest structure and moisture. Geometric patches illustrate where canopy disturbance might shift the backscatter distribution. Compare HV to explore vegetation scattering.
phenomena.limitation: These patches are invented. Moisture, flooding, and processing differences can mimic forest change; real loss needs independent validation.
